author: Garrett Ball
title: Josh Green traded to Minnesota Timberwolves
desc: Josh Green has been traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves as a part of a larger deal that sees LaMelo Ball go to Minnesota and Naz Reid and a host of picks return to Charlotte.
impact: Green isn't a game changing player but he is a nice depth option for when the team needs him. Don't expect him to get a ton of playing time, but he could find himself in some spot starts where he'd become fantasy relevant.

author: Garrett Ball
title: Naz Reid traded to Charlotte Hornets
desc: Naz Reid has been traded to the Charlotte Hornets along with a 2033 first round pick, three first round swaps, and three second round picks for LaMelo Ball and Josh Green.
impact: The Wolves needed a point guard and they now have their man. As for the Hornets, as a former Sixth Man of the Year, Naz is capable on offense though not prolific, and his defense can be suspect at times. However, he fills a need for the Hornets in giving them a good veteran option at the power forward spot as they look to get their youth up and running at guard and center.

author: Garrett Ball
title: LaMelo Ball traded to Minnesota Timberwolves
desc: LaMelo Ball has been traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves for Naz Reid, a 2033 first round pick, three first round pick swaps, and three second round picks. Charlotte is also sending Josh Green to Minnesota.
impact: This is a massive trade for the Hornets who are coming off of a promising year with their young core. Now that will need to be rebuilt, and LaMelo will look to give the Timberwolves a fierce backcourt duo alongside Anthony Edwards. He won't be the No.1 option for a team anymore, but Ant should open things up for LaMelo on offense.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Tobe Awaka signs two-way deal with Bulls
desc: Undrafted Arizona forward Tobe Awaka has agreed to a two-way NBA deal with the Chicago Bulls.
impact: Awaka was one of the bigger surprises to go undrafted. He was one of the top offensive rebounders in college basketball at Arizona. He'll look to prove himself in Summer League action.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Tre Donaldson signs two-way deal with Heat
desc: Undrafted Miami guard Tre Donaldson has agreed to a two-way NBA deal with the Miami Heat.
impact: Donaldson will get a chance to prove himself in the Summer League in July. He averaged a career-high 16 points per game in his lone season at Miami last year.

author: Diego Sandoval
title: Isaiah Stewart traded to Memphis Grizzlies
desc: Isaiah Stewart is being traded to the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for three future second-round picks.
impact: It was revealed that Stewart was available for trade last week, and the big man is now heading to Memphis. The 25-year-old is coming off a season where he averaged 10 points and five rebounds a game while playing 22.7 minutes per night. He will give the Grizzlies a solid frontcourt depth piece.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Pelle Larsson has team option exercised by Heat
desc: The Miami Heat have exercised the team option on G Pelle Larsson.
impact: Larsson took a step forward in his second season last year and following the blockbuster trade Miami made, he could step into an even bigger role off the bench for Miami this upcoming season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Austin Reaves intends to sign four-year max contract with Lakers
desc: Austin Reaves intends to sign a four-year, $185 million maximum contract to return to the Lakers.
impact: The deal will include a player option for the final season in 2029-30. Reaves declined his $14.9 million player option for the new max deal. It is officially the richest contract for an undrafted player in NBA history. The next step for the Lakers will be to see if they re-sign LeBron James in free agency.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Sergio de Larrea traded to Mavericks
desc: The Knicks traded No. 25 pick Sergio De Larrea to the Dallas Mavericks for No. 30 Koa Peat and two second-round picks.
impact: Peat is on the move to the Suns. De Larrea was drafted by the Lakers, traded to the Knicks and now on the move again to Dallas where he'll figure to be a long-term project.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Koa Peat selected No. 30 overall by Mavericks, traded to Suns
desc: Koa Peat has been selected No. 30 overall by the Mavericks in the 2026 NBA Draft. He will be traded to the Suns.
impact: After playing both high school and college basketball in the state of Arizona, Peat is staying home in Arizona to play for the Suns. He holds the size and physicality to make an immediate impact at the next level, but it is his outside shooting that he'll need to work on and develop.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Alex Karaban selected No. 29 overall by Cavaliers, traded to Kings
desc: Alex Karaban has been selected No. 29 overall by the Cavaliers in the 2026 NBA Draft. He will be traded to the Kings.
impact: Karaban had a historic collegiate career at UConn where he won two national championships. He'll bring his winning resume and sharpshooting ability from the outside to Sacramento.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Joshua Jefferson selected No. 28 overall by Timberwolves, traded to Nets
desc: Joshua Jefferson has been selected No. 28 overall by the Timberwolves in the 2026 NBA Draft. He will be traded to the Nets.
impact: This pick is going to Brooklyn as part of the Julius Randle trade. Jefferson is a forward who can do a bit of everything as a scorer, passer and rebounder with physicality. He'll add to the young core of Brooklyn.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Chris Cenac Jr. selected No. 27 overall by Celtics
desc: Chris Cenac Jr. has been selected No. 27 overall by the Celtics in the 2026 NBA Draft.
impact: Cenac showed flashes of his upside as a freshman last season as a stretch four. He added six double-doubles as he crashed the boards all season under coach Kelvin Sampson. He holds the ability to make an immediate impact for Boston as a rookie.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Tarris Reed Jr. selected No. 26 overall by Nuggets, traded to Spurs
desc: Tarris Reed Jr. has been selected No. 26 overall by the Nuggets in the 2026 NBA Draft. He will be traded to the Spurs.
impact: Reed was a double-double machine during last season at UConn. He'll add more size and physicality off the bench for a deep Spurs rotation.
